nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, egg, ham, sausage and cheese.

citations.source: Excélsior, Cómo hacer torta cubana tradicional
La Razón, Qué lleva la torta cubana y por qué se le dice así

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior for the teleras, beef milanesas, Vienna sausages, ham, Oaxaca or manchego, fried egg, avocado, tomato, onion, beans, mayonnaise, mustard and pickled chiles, milanesa 3 to 4 minutes a side and 2 minutes pressed on the plancha, doubled here to 4 tortas; La Razón for the name coming from Calle de Cuba in the Centro Histórico rather than the island, and for torterías that add pierna, quesillo or egg with chorizo. Cooked ham, Vienna sausages and bread crumbs are not in the database. The oil row counts what the milanesas and eggs absorb.

recipes.name: Pambazo
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft bread bathed in red guajillo sauce and fried in lard, filled with potato mashed into chorizo, then topped with lettuce, cream, aged cheese and green salsa.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potato gives potassium and vitamin C, guajillo chile adds vitamin A, and the lettuce and raw salsa bring freshness to a street food fried in lard.

components.note: standing in for pan bazo, a soft white roll; a day-old roll takes the sauce best

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and cut in large pieces

instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water 15 to 20 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Cook the chorizo in a skillet over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes, until it releases its fat. Add the potatoes, mash them into the chorizo and cook 3 minutes more. Season with salt if needed.
Split the rolls, leaving one side joined, and fill with the potato and chorizo.

Heat some of the lard in a skillet over medium heat. Brush or dip the outside of each filled roll in the guajillo sauce, top side first, and set it in the pan. Brush the other side and fry 1 to 2 minutes a side, until the sauce sets and darkens, adding lard as needed.
Open each pambazo and add lettuce, cream, crumbled cheese and green salsa. Serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the guajillo sauce and lettuce.

citations.source: Por Esto, Receta para preparar pambazos
México Desconocido, Pambazo
Directo al Paladar, Pambazos de patata y chorizo

recipes.curationNote: Por Esto for 8 pambazos, a thick guajillo sauce, 2 cups chorizo with 3 potatoes mashed in, ¼ cup lard for frying face down, and lettuce, crema, queso añejo and raw green salsa; México Desconocido for the Mexico City pambazo dipped in guajillo and fried, potato with chorizo or longaniza, and pan bazo as a white bread from Castile; Directo al Paladar for brushing the sauce on the outside of the bread before toasting. Pan bazo is not one of the shared bases, so the bolillo stands in.

recipes.name: Enchiladas Rojas
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft corn tortillas dipped in brick-red guajillo sauce and rolled around shredded chicken, finished with cream, fresh cheese, onion, lettuce and radish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives lean protein, corn tortillas whole-grain fiber, and guajillo chiles carotenoids, with fresh vegetables piled on top.
instructions: Heat the guajillo sauce in a wide pan over medium heat with 1 tbsp of the oil and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until it coats a spoon.
Brush the tortillas lightly with the remaining oil and warm them on a comal about 30 seconds a side, until pliable. Keep them wrapped in a cloth.
Dip each tortilla in the hot sauce, fill with about 3 tbsp of chicken, roll and lay seam side down on warm plates, 3 to a plate.
Spoon more sauce over, then top with crema, queso fresco, onion, lettuce, radish and avocado. Serve with lime at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: Guajillo chiles are rich in carotenoids.
From the corn tortillas and avocado.

citations.source: MexGrocer, Enchiladas rojas from scratch with guajillo sauce
Camila Made, Enchiladas rojas de queso

recipes.curationNote: MexGrocer for 4 servings of 12 enchiladas, 2 cups shredded chicken or queso fresco, the sauce simmered 8 to 10 minutes in a tablespoon of oil, tortillas brushed with oil and warmed, and crema, queso fresco, onion, lettuce, radish, avocado and lime on top; Camila Made for the cheese filling as the other common version and for dipping each tortilla before rolling. The oil row counts what the tortillas take up.

recipes.name: Enfrijoladas
recipes.flavorProfile: Tortillas softened in oil and folded through a smooth black bean sauce scented with avocado leaf and a touch of chile de árbol, under melting string cheese and onion.
recipes.healthBenefit: Black beans bring fiber, folate, plant protein and polyphenols, and with corn tortillas they make a complete protein in a humble, filling plate.

components.note: black beans with their broth, about 2 cups beans and 2½ cups broth

instructions: Toast the chile de árbol and avocado leaves on a dry comal 15 to 30 seconds, until fragrant. Blend with the beans and their broth about 30 seconds, until smooth.

Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the bean purée and cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring. It should be about as thick as heavy cream; loosen with water ¼ cup (60 ml) at a time if needed. Season with salt.
Heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over medium heat and pass each tortilla through it 10 to 20 seconds a side, just until soft. Drain on paper.
Dip each tortilla in the hot sauce about 15 seconds a side, fold in half and lay 3 on each plate. Spoon about ⅓ cup (80 ml) more sauce over, top with the cheeses, onion and parsley, and serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: Black beans are among the richest everyday sources.
From the cheeses and the lime-treated corn tortillas.

citations.source: I Love Mole (Guelaguetza), Enfrijoladas
Excélsior, Historia de las enfrijoladas
La Opinión, Así se preparan las auténticas enfrijoladas mexicanas

recipes.curationNote: Guelaguetza (via I Love Mole) for 4 plates of 3, the toasted árbol blended with 2 cups beans and 2½ cups broth, tortillas fried 10 to 20 seconds a side, dipped 15 seconds, and Oaxaca cheese or low-moisture mozzarella with queso fresco, onion and parsley; Excélsior for the Oaxacan sauce of black beans with epazote and avocado leaves and the regional versions; La Opinión for warming the tortillas in oil without crisping them. recipes.name: Enmoladas
recipes.flavorProfile: Folded tortillas filled with chicken and smothered in dark, sweet-spiced mole poblano, topped with cream, crumbled cheese and raw onion.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mole carries chiles, seeds, nuts and spices full of polyphenols and minerals, and the chicken adds lean protein.
instructions: Heat the mole with the broth in a saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring, 5 to 8 minutes, until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and pass each tortilla through it a few seconds a side, so it softens without crisping.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, fold in half and lay 3 on each plate.
Pour the hot mole over to cover completely, then top with crema, queso fresco and onion. Serve hot, with rice or refried beans if you like.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the seeds, nuts and chocolate in the mole.
From the dried chiles and seeds in the mole.

Directo al Paladar, Enchiladas de pollo con mole poblano

The base mole is already a finished sauce, so only ½ cup broth is added. The oil row counts what the tortillas take up.

recipes.name: Entomatadas
recipes.flavorProfile: Tortillas bathed in a mild, oregano-scented tomato sauce and folded around fresh cheese and onion, with a little cream on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, mild plate: cooked tomato gives lycopene and vitamin C, and the corn tortillas and fresh cheese add fiber, calcium and protein.

components.note: crumbled, part for filling and part for the top

instructions: Bring the tomato sauce to a simmer in a wide pan with a little of the oil and keep it hot.
Warm the tortillas on a comal or brush them with the rest of the oil and heat 15 to 20 seconds a side, so they do not tear when dipped.
Dip each tortilla in the sauce, fill with crumbled cheese and onion, fold in half and lay 3 on each plate.
Spoon a little broth and more sauce over, then top with the remaining cheese, a little crema and cilantro. Serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the queso fresco and the corn tortillas.

citations.source: Cookpad, Entomatadas
TV Azteca, La receta de la chef Zahie Téllez

recipes.curationNote: Cookpad for the tomato sauce with oregano, tortillas bathed and fried, filled with onion and queso oreado, and finished with a little broth, cheese and crema; Zahie Téllez for frying the sauce, keeping the tortillas warm so they do not break, and queso fresco with cream or cilantro on top. Queso fresco from the base stands in for queso oreado.

recipes.name: Flautas de Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: Long, tight rolls of tortilla around chicken cooked with tomato, chile and cumin, fried golden and crackling, then heaped with lettuce, cream, cheese and green salsa.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean chicken in a tomato and chile filling, served under fresh lettuce and radish; frying adds fat, so they are best with plenty of vegetables on the side.
instructions: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and chile 1 minute, add the tomato, chipotle, cumin and salt and cook until saucy, 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in the chicken and cilantro and cook about 5 minutes, until little liquid is left.
Warm the tortillas on a comal until pliable and keep them wrapped. Lay a line of filling along one edge of each, roll tightly and secure with a toothpick or keep seam side down.

Heat about 1 inch (2.5 cm) of oil in a large pan to 350°F (175°C). Fry the flautas seam side down first, in batches, about 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain on paper and pull out the toothpicks.
Plate 4 per person and top with lettuce, radish, crema, cheese and green salsa. Serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomato, chile and salsa verde.

citations.source: Maricruz Avalos, Flautas de pollo
Directo al Paladar, Flautas de pollo

recipes.curationNote: Maricruz Avalos for 16 flautas, 4 a plate, 2 cups chicken cooked with tomato, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, chipotle and cumin, rolled tight, fried in about 1 inch of oil, and lettuce, radish, crema and queso fresco on top; Directo al Paladar for frying seam side down about 3 minutes a side and green salsa with cream and cheese. Neither gives an oil temperature, so 350°F is the usual frying heat. Chipotle is not in the database. The deep-fried oil row counts what the flautas absorb, not the pan.

recipes.name: Chilaquiles Rojos
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp fried tortilla chips tossed in a hot red guajillo and árbol sauce just long enough to soak at the edges, under a fried egg, cream, cheese, onion and avocado.
recipes.healthBenefit: The tomato and chile sauce brings vitamin C and carotenoids, the egg protein, and the avocado healthy fat, in a breakfast that keeps people going.

ingredients.cutPrep: a piece for the sauce, the rest finely chopped

instructions: Simmer the guajillo and árbol chiles, tomatoes, garlic and a piece of the onion in water to cover over medium heat about 10 minutes, until the chiles soften and the tomatoes change color.
Drain and blend with 1 cup (240 ml) of the broth, the cumin, oregano, salt and pepper until smooth, adding more broth if it is very thick.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat, pour in the sauce and cook 5 minutes, until it thickens slightly. Add the remaining broth as needed.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in the other tablespoon of oil.
Add the totopos to the hot sauce and fold gently, 1 minute for crunchy or 3 to 4 minutes for soft. Plate at once with an egg on each, then crema, cheese, chopped onion, cilantro and avocado.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomato and chile sauce.
Guajillo chiles are rich in carotenoids.

citations.source: El Universal, Receta: cómo preparar chilaquiles rojos
Excélsior, Prepara los mejores chilaquiles rojos con la receta tradicional

recipes.curationNote: El Universal for 12 tortillas or 300 g totopos, 7 guajillo and 3 árbol chiles, 3 tomatoes, 2 cups chicken broth, garlic, onion, cumin, oregano, 4 fried eggs, avocado, crema, queso fresco, onion and cilantro, and adding the chips just before serving for crunch; Excélsior for drying the tortillas overnight, boiling the chiles and tomatoes 10 minutes and thickening the sauce 5 minutes in a little oil. Guajillo and árbol are not in the database.

recipes.name: Chile Relleno
recipes.flavorProfile: A roasted poblano stuffed with melting cheese, wrapped in a puffed egg batter and fried golden, then simmered briefly in a thin tomato caldillo with marjoram and thyme.
recipes.healthBenefit: Poblano chiles are rich in vitamin C and the tomato caldillo adds more, with cheese and egg for protein and calcium; the frying makes it a dish for now and then.

ingredients.name: pan molido (dry bread crumbs)
ingredients.prepNote: about 3 tbsp, to thicken the caldillo

instructions: Roast the poblanos over a flame or on a comal until the skin is black on all sides. Seal them in a bag for 20 to 30 minutes to sweat, then rub off the skin, rinse briefly and pat dry.
Cut a slit down one side of each chile and pull out the seeds and veins. Fill with cheese without overstuffing so the chile closes; pin with a toothpick if needed.

For the caldillo, roast the tomatoes, onion and garlic, blend and strain. Simmer in 1 tbsp oil over low heat 10 minutes, stir in the bread crumbs, add the broth, marjoram and thyme and simmer 15 minutes over medium-low heat. Season with salt.
Separate the eggs. Beat the whites to firm peaks, then fold in the yolks one at a time without knocking out the air.

Heat about 1 inch (2.5 cm) of oil to 340 to 355°F (170 to 180°C). Dust each chile in flour, dip it in the batter and fry one or two at a time, spooning oil over the top, until golden underneath. Turn once and brown the other side. Drain on paper.
Set the chiles in the caldillo and simmer 2 minutes, or ladle the caldillo into plates and set a chile in each. Serve at once with rice and warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the poblano and the tomato caldillo.

citations.source: Excélsior, Chiles rellenos de queso capeados
Directo al Paladar, Chiles rellenos de queso, receta tradicional mexicana

recipes.curationNote: Excélsior for 6 large poblanos, 300 g Oaxaca or manchego, 3 eggs, ½ cup flour, sweating 20 minutes, whites beaten to peaks with the yolks folded in, frying at 170 to 180°C one or two at a time, and a caldillo of tomato, onion and garlic; Directo al Paladar for 5 eggs, roasting the tomatoes, thickening the caldillo with 3 tbsp bread crumbs, 2 cups chicken broth, marjoram and thyme simmered 15 minutes, and a final 2 minutes of the chiles in the caldillo. Eggs set at 4 between the two. Poblano, Oaxaca cheese and bread crumbs are not in the database, so asadero stands in for the cheese. The frying oil row counts what the batter absorbs.

recipes.name: Pollo en Mole Poblano
recipes.flavorProfile: Pieces of poached chicken warmed through in dark, glossy mole poblano, sweet with chocolate and spice and gently hot, under a scatter of toasted sesame.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives protein, and the mole carries dried chiles, sesame, almonds, peanuts and spices that bring fiber, minerals and polyphenols to the plate.

components.note: from poaching the chicken, to loosen the mole

instructions: Put the chicken in a pot with the onion, garlic, salt and water to cover. Bring to a boil, skim, then lower the heat and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, until cooked through to 165°F (74°C). Keep the broth.
Warm the mole in a wide cazuela over low heat, stirring, and loosen it with about ½ cup (120 ml) of the broth until it coats a spoon thickly.
Add the chicken pieces and simmer gently 10 to 15 minutes, turning them in the sauce, until hot and glossy.
Plate one or two pieces per person with plenty of mole, sprinkle with toasted sesame and serve with red rice and warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sesame, nuts and chocolate in the mole.

citations.source: TV Azteca, Mole con pollo, el paso a paso de Isabel Carvajal en MasterChef
Food and Pleasure, Recetas de mole poblano
MedlinePlus, Pollo con mole

recipes.curationNote: TV Azteca (MasterChef) for 4 pieces of chicken boiled with salt, one piece per plate with toasted sesame and red or white rice; Food and Pleasure for leg pieces cooked in salted water and then cooked on in the finished mole until glossy; MedlinePlus for poaching about 30 minutes to 165°F and the tradition of sesame over the chicken and sauce. The base mole is already a finished sauce, so only broth is added here.

recipes.name: Mole Negro con Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: Chicken simmered in Oaxaca's near-black mole, smoky from burnt chiles, bittersweet with chocolate and fragrant with avocado leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: A protein-rich plate whose sauce is built from chiles, seeds, nuts, plantain and chocolate, a dense mix of minerals and polyphenols.
instructions: Bring the water, onion, garlic, bay leaf and pepper to a boil in a large pot, add the chicken and return to a boil. Lower the heat, cover and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the juices of the dark meat run clear. Add the salt and keep the broth.
Heat the mole in a cazuela over low heat, stirring so it does not stick, and thin it with broth if it is very thick.
Add the chicken and simmer 15 minutes, turning the pieces in the sauce.
Set a piece of chicken on each plate, pour plenty of hot mole over and serve with white rice and warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dried chiles and seeds in the mole.
From the nuts, seeds and chocolate.

citations.source: Ya Oaxaca, Turkey or chicken with mole negro sauce
Cookpad, Mole negro oaxaqueño

recipes.curationNote: Ya Oaxaca for 4 servings from about 3½ lb bone-in chicken parts simmered 45 minutes to 1 hour with onion, garlic, bay and peppercorns, salt added at the end, the hot mole poured over a piece on each plate and rice with tortillas alongside; Cookpad for a whole chicken poached with onion, garlic and salt and the pieces simmered 15 minutes in the finished mole. The base mole is already a finished sauce.

recipes.name: Mole Verde con Cerdo
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender pork in a bright green sauce of pumpkin seed, tomatillo, hoja santa, epazote and fresh herbs, with chayote and green beans cooked just tender.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pumpkin seeds and leafy herbs give magnesium, zinc and vitamin K, the vegetables add fiber and vitamin C, and pork shoulder brings protein and B vitamins.

components.note: finished sauce, kept off the boil

instructions: Put the pork in a pot with the onion, garlic, salt and water to cover. Bring to a boil, skim, then cover and simmer over low heat 1½ to 2 hours, until tender.
Boil the chayote, green beans and zucchini separately in salted water until just tender, 5 to 10 minutes each. Drain.

Warm the mole verde in a cazuela over low heat, loosening it with a little of the pork broth if needed. Add the pork and vegetables and heat through 5 to 8 minutes without letting it boil hard, so the sauce keeps its green color.
Serve in bowls or deep plates with warm tortillas or totopos.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pumpkin seeds are among the richest sources.
From the herbs and leafy greens in the sauce.

citations.source: México Desconocido, Mole verde con carne
La Opinión, Prepara un exquisito mole verde veracruzano

recipes.curationNote: México Desconocido for pork leg or loin cooked with onion, garlic and salt until soft, then warmed in the finished green mole, keeping part of the herb sauce back so it is not boiled and stays green, served with totopos; La Opinión (from Larousse) for 6 servings from 1¼ kg pork, and chayote, green beans and zucchini boiled separately in salted water before going into the mole. Shoulder is used here as the cut that stays most tender with long simmering.

recipes.name: Mole Amarillo con Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: The lightest of the Oaxacan moles: chicken, chayote and green beans in a thin, masa-thickened sauce of guajillo, tomato and tomatillo perfumed with hoja santa.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken for protein and chayote, green beans and potato for fiber, potassium and vitamin C, in a sauce with little fat compared with the darker moles.

ingredients.cutPrep: thinly sliced, macerated in lime juice and salt

instructions: Put the chicken in a pot with the onion, garlic, salt and water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until cooked through to 165°F (74°C). Keep the broth.

Cover the potatoes with water, bring to a boil, then cook covered over medium heat 10 minutes. Add the chayote and cook 5 minutes, then add the green beans and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until they are bright green and the potatoes are fork tender. Drain.
Toss the sliced onion with the lime juice and a pinch of salt and leave it to soften while you finish the dish.
Heat the mole in a pot over medium-low heat, thinning with a little broth if needed. Add the chicken and simmer 10 minutes to heat through, then add the vegetables for the last 2 to 3 minutes.
Ladle into deep plates with a piece of chicken and some of each vegetable, and top with the lime onions. Serve with warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chayote, green beans, potato and tomatoes in the sauce.

citations.source: My Slice of Mexico, Oaxaca style yellow mole
Rick Bayless, Chicken breasts with yellow mole and roasted vegetables

recipes.curationNote: My Slice of Mexico for a cut-up chicken cooked in water with its broth kept, potatoes cooked 10 minutes, chayote 5 more and green beans a couple of minutes, and the bowls topped with onions macerated in lime and salt; Rick Bayless for 4 servings with about 4 cups of sauce, chayote and green beans as the vegetables, and the chicken reheated in the finished mole. The chochoyotes some cooks add are left out here.

recipes.name: Mole Coloradito con Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: Chicken and potatoes simmered in brick-red coloradito, sweet with plantain, egg bread and Oaxacan chocolate over ancho chile, finished with toasted sesame.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives protein and the potatoes potassium, while the ancho chiles and sesame in the sauce add carotenoids and minerals.

ingredients.cutPrep: crushed with salt and oregano into a paste

instructions: Rub the chicken with the garlic paste, salt and oregano and refrigerate 1 to 12 hours.
Put the chicken in a large pot with the onion, the rest of the garlic and salt and water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, until barely tender. Keep the broth.
Boil the potatoes in salted water 12 to 15 minutes, until tender. Drain.

Heat the mole in a heavy pot over medium heat with ½ cup (120 ml) of broth and simmer 5 minutes. Add the chicken and potatoes, with more broth if it is very thick, and simmer gently 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Serve in a clay cazuela or deep plates, sprinkled with toasted sesame, with refried beans, rice and warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: Ancho chiles are rich in carotenoids.

citations.source: México Desconocido, Receta de pollo en mole coloradito
AARP en Español, Mole coloradito de guajolote

recipes.curationNote: México Desconocido for chicken boiled with onion and garlic until soft, cooked potatoes added to the mole with more broth and simmered 10 minutes, served in a cazuela with refried beans and rice; AARP for chicken legs and thighs rubbed with garlic, salt and oregano 1 to 12 hours, poached 25 to 30 minutes, the paste thinned with broth 5 minutes, the chicken simmered 10 minutes and sesame on top. The base mole is already a finished sauce.

recipes.name: Pipián Verde con Pollo
recipes.flavorProfile: Chicken simmered in a creamy, pale green sauce of toasted pumpkin and sesame seeds, tomatillo, green chile and fresh herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: The pumpkin seed sauce is rich in magnesium, zinc and healthy fats, and the chicken brings lean protein.
instructions: Put the chicken in a pot with the onion, garlic, salt and water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer 30 to 40 minutes, until cooked through to 165°F (74°C). Keep the broth.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat, add the pipián and bring it just to a boil, stirring. If it is thicker than heavy cream, loosen it with broth.
Add the chicken, lower the heat, cover and simmer 10 to 15 minutes so the chicken takes up the sauce, without letting it boil hard or the seeds will split.
Serve hot with white rice and warm tortillas.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pumpkin seeds are among the richest sources.
Also from the pumpkin seeds and the chicken.

La Cocina de Leslie, Chicken pipián verde
